eSource@ENRON (40enron@enron.com) sent the most messages on 2001-09-05. It sent 23 that day, out of 160 messages from that address in September 2001. The next busiest days were 2001-09-28 with 19 and 2001-09-14 with 16.

I filtered on the sender address and counted messages by their UTC date.

ANSWER: 2001-09-05
SOURCES: E80e4adf85ec0

Angelic Davis (angelic.davis@enron.com) sent 6 unique messages to dana.davis@enron.com between 2001-10-01 and 2001-11-01 (end exclusive). I filtered by sender, recipient (To or Cc) and date range. All 6 message ids were distinct, so no duplicates needed removing. I printed only five of the six ids, so the sources below are those five.

ANSWER: 6
SOURCES: Eec51ca95dc10, E78c208665714, Ea4671be47808, Ea9e43a0d11aa, Ef703ce92e611

Jeff Dasovich sent the most messages to Richard Sanders in that window. I filtered for messages with richard.sanders@enron.com in To or Cc, dated 2001-05-29 up to but not including 2001-06-05. That gave 37 messages, and Dasovich sent 8 of them. Susan Mara was next with 5, then Janette Elbertson with 4.

ANSWER: jeff.dasovich@enron.com
SOURCES: Ec64a0fe2fe15, Efbeffae21bed, Eb4461cb03bfd, E89c6a95fd0e2, Eaa28b1519008

In April 2001 (UTC), Vince Kaminski sent the most messages to vkaminski@aol.com. I counted 173 unique messages to that address, in To or Cc, out of 458 messages he sent that month. The next most frequent recipient was his own Enron address, vince.kaminski@enron.com, with 135. After that came shirley.crenshaw@enron.com with 54.

The sender filter matches on a substring of the address or display name. I didn't check whether it pulled in any messages from other senders.

ANSWER: vkaminski@aol.com
SOURCES:

I counted messages from vince.kaminski@enron.com between 2001-04-01 and 2001-05-01, grouped by UTC date. I didn't open any individual messages, so I have no specific message IDs to cite.

ANSWER: 2001-04-25
SOURCES:

The only message that mentions 703-227-8777 is **Ef817f5aac97c**. It was sent on 2001-08-24 with the subject "FW: 082501 Enron Confirmation". The number appears in the message as "703.227.8777 Phone". The sender is Bryant Frihart, at bryant.frihart@enron.com.

I searched the full text of every message with a pattern that allows dashes, dots or spaces between the digit groups. It returned exactly one match.

ANSWER: bryant.frihart@enron.com
SOURCES: Ef817f5aac97c

The reference ORE-7509 appears in one message, **E2083b9620d07**. Its subject is "(CMS-26) NOTICE OF INTENTION TO TRANSFER MEMBERSHIP", and it was sent on 2002-02-27.

The sender is marketing@nymex.com, with the display name "Exchange Information @ENRON". The matching line reads "Edward Orenchuk (ORE-7509)", so the reference seems to be tied to a person named in the notice. The message came from the deleted_items folder of custodian shackleton-s.

ANSWER: marketing@nymex.com
SOURCES: E2083b9620d07

The only message that mentions EB-2934 is E2093dccd9417. Robin Barbe (robin.barbe@enron.com) sent it on 2000-12-05, and its subject is "PSEG Meeting". It went to Chris Germany and Dick Jenkins. The matching line reads "50,000/d @ Transco Zone 6, on Tuesday, December 5, 3:00 p.m., in EB-2934." In that line, EB-2934 appears to be a meeting room.

ANSWER: robin.barbe@enron.com
SOURCES: E2093dccd9417
